newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, marks, Swiss francs down.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, marks, Swiss francs down.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mixed as Swiss francs tumbled in sympathy with marks and Canadian dollars firmed, traders said.
Several futures traders attributed the late decline in December marks to comments by John Whitehead, chairman of the board of directors at the New York Federal Reserve Bank.
"There is no question those comments bolstered the dollar," said Dave Durrant, senior currency analyst at I.D.E.A. Inc. "And we could see follow-through (dollar buying) tomorrow."
According to a wire-service report, Whitehead said the dollar has room to appreciate five to 10 percent against European currencies.
Mark futures, which were already on the defense due to cash cross weakness, slipped to their daily low at $0.6552 in the December contract.

The dollar/mark's rally above the 3-1/2-month high of 1.5318 spot, or $0.6559, paved the way for a re-test of its four-month high at 1.5383, which roughly corresponds to $0.6532 in December, traders said. December's contract low is currently at $0.6537.
The weakness in mark futures added pressure to Swiss franc futures, which opened the day on the positive side.

December Swiss francs fell to $0.8007, through their three-month low set on Monday at $0.8010. Support is seen at $0.8004, which is equivalent to key resistance in the dollar/Swiss franc at 1.2600 spot.
One technical analyst said both December marks and Swiss francs were trading in ranges, but at the lower end of those ranges.
"Technically, marks are in a big range, but they are looking soft within that range," he said.

One major U.S. investment house bought 2,500 December Canadian dollar futures, while another U.S. firm bought 1,200 in the afternoon. December, which held support at $0.7364 after the rate cut, ended near the $0.7379 level.

One firm bought December yen, which helped keep the contract off its lows, traders said. They also noted good retail buying in Mexican pesos. At the end of pit trade, December yen off $0.000042 at $0.009029, marks off $0.0032 at $0.6555, Swiss francs off $0.0027 at $0.8013, sterling up $0.0004 at $1.5644, Can dollars up $0.0003 at $0.7379, Aussie dollars up $0.0031 at $0.7933, pesos up $0.000125 at $0.127300. Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuter.com
Cash marks remained on the defensive on the crosses, particularly against Italian lira, as comments by various officials were mostly supportive towards the European Monetary Union, analysts said.
The declines in the cash mark crosses also lent support to the dollar, as foreign investors continued to pour money into the U.S., they said.

Positive flows into the U.S. benefited Canadian dollar futures, with December firming into the close. Although the Bank of Canada lowered its key bank rate by 25 basis points to four percent, several firms were large buyers of futures.
